newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes a tad firmer after wobbly trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes a tad firmer after wobbly trade.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly firmer on Wednesday after seesawing during a session hallmarked by speculation and lack of dollars, traders said.
"The financial markets still don't look stable to me...we still have jitters and speculation that cause sudden shifts in the exchange rate," said one trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.35 and 0.7 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9090/7.9140 and 7.9030/7.9080 per dollar.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 2.25 centavos weaker at 7.9080/7.9125. Same-day peso trading closes three hours before the other contracts, and therefore lagged behind the recovery.
The peso had opened weak, in response to mixed results at Tuesday night's primary Cetes auction, but soon the anxiety faded and allowed the peso to recover.
Traders said sources of speculation were the Mexican government's forthcoming budget proposals, due Thursday, local elections on Sunday, and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on November 13.
"I'm still convinced we could see year lows (for the peso) in the next two weeks," said another trader.
